newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: At least two killed at Pakistan independence rally.
newsitem.headline: At least two killed at Pakistan independence rally.

text.p: At least two people were killed and 20 wounded when a crowd stampeded at a rally for Pakistan's independence day on Thursday, witnesses said.

They said at least two people had been killed and three wounded in gunfire when police retaliated for shots fired from the crowd. The other casualties were hurt in a police baton charge or were trampled underfoot when people panicked.
The trouble erupted during a rally at the mausoleum of Pakistan's founder Mohammad Ali Jinnah to mark the Islamic nation's 50th anniversary of independence from Britain.
President Farooq Leghari and Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif were unhurt, but witnesses said several government officials had to fight their way past hostile crowds after the baton charge.

One official said the trouble among the crowd estimated at 20,000 had begun when Sharif had said people should be allowed to come forward. "Security is in the hands of God. Let the people come close," Sharif was quoted as saying.
The crowd then broke through police cordons and rushed towards the podium amid the shrieks of women and children as dozens of people fell and were trampled underfoot.
